L45: # Quantitative Persistence and Regularity of Invariant Graphs for Dissipative Twist Maps
L46: Deyu Kong Address: School of Mathematics and Statistics, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing 100081, China Email address: dykong@bit.edu.cn , Jessica Elisa Massetti Address: Department of Mathematics, University of Rome Tor Vergata, Via della ricerca scientifica 1, 00133 Rome, Italy Email address: massetti@axp.mat.uniroma2.it and Lin Wang Address: School of Mathematics and Statistics, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing 100081, China Email address: lwang@bit.edu.cn
L47: ###### Abstract.
L48: In this paper we study the robustness of invariant Lagrangian graphs for dissipative twist maps on $\mathbb{T}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d}$ in the $C^{r}$ category, for any $r\geq 1$, and show their persistence as invariant global attractors under quantitative sharp conditions involving both the size of dissipation parameter and the perturbation at stake. Note that when $d>1$ the geometric Lagrangian property of the invariant manifold may be destroyed, so that the graph may persist but fail to be Lagrangian.
L49: In general, additional dynamical requirements on the twist maps come into play if we intend to preserve also the Lagrangian property. In this line, we first study their persistence for general perturbations, then we restrict to the class of exact conformally symplectic twist maps and provide quantitative sharp conditions for the persistence of invariant exact Lagrangian graphs, without assuming any condition on the tangential dynamics of the manifold.
L50: The persistence result relies on a combination of a suitable multidimensional Herman–Mather formula proved in this setting and contraction estimates that provide sharp bounds on the $C^{1}$-norm of the perturbation to get a unique, globally attracting $C^{r}$ graph. In dimension $d=1$, by further assuming that that the circle map induced by the graph has irrational rotation number, we prove that every $C^{1}$ invariant graph of a $C^{k}$ map is $C^{k}$ for $k=2,3,\ldots,\infty$.
L51: Analytic maps with Lipschitz, non-$C^{1}$ invariant graphs at every prescribed irrational rotation number show that this initial regularity assumption is essential.

L86: ## 1. Introduction and main results
L87: 
L88: We study invariant graphs for dissipative twist maps on $\mathbb{T}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d}$, $d\geq 1$, whose lifts have the form
L89: 
L90: (1)  |  | $$F_{\Lambda,\alpha}^{\phi}(x,y)=\bigl(x+\alpha_{1}+\Lambda_{1}y+\phi_{1}(x),\,\alpha_{2}+\Lambda_{2}y+\phi_{2}(x)\bigr).$$  |
L91: Here $\alpha=(\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2})\in\mathbb{R}^{2d}$, $\Lambda_{1},\Lambda_{2}\in GL_{d}(\mathbb{R})$, and the perturbations $\phi_{1},\phi_{2}:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{d}$ are $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$-periodic. We assume that $F_{\Lambda,\alpha}^{\phi}$ is a global diffeomorphism and that its projection $f_{\Lambda,\alpha}^{\phi}$ on the cylinder is isotopic to the identity and satisfies
L92: 
L93: (2)  |  | $$0<\det DF_{\Lambda,\alpha}^{\phi}(x,y)<1.$$  |
L94: Periodicity gives the lift relation $F(x+k,y)=F(x,y)+(k,0)$ for $k\in\mathbb{Z}^{d}$. The full conventions are given in Definition 【33†2.3】. Our main contraction assumption is
L95: 
L96: (3)  |  | $$M:=\Lambda_{1}\Lambda_{2}\Lambda_{1}^{-1},\qquad\|M\|<1,$$  |
L97: where $\|\cdot\|$ stands for the operator norm induced by the standard euclidean metric on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$. We seek explicit conditions under which an invariant graph exists, determine its regularity, and ask when it is Lagrangian.
L98: We stress the fact that in dimension greater than $2$, the Lagrangian property is not automatically preserved together with the invariant graph and there exist cases where the invariant graph persists, but its Lagrangian property is destroyed by the perturbation (see Section 【19†4】). This geometric property is kept only under further conditions on the admissible perturbations or on under dynamical hypothesis of the system at stake (see Section 【6†1.2】).
L99: For this reason we shall treat the two matters separately and distinguish between a more general result on existence of $C^{k}$-invariant graph and one of invariant Lagrangian graph, where we shall restrict to the class of exact conformally sympletic twist map, the geometric property being more involved.
L100: The study of attracting invariant sets for dissipative annulus maps goes back to Birkhoff [【34†Bir32】]. Later work established periodic orbits for dissipative twist maps [【35†Cas87】] and quasi-periodic orbits in Birkhoff attractors [【36†LeC86】]. Arnaud, Humilière, and Viterbo [【37†AHV26】] extended the notion of a Birkhoff attractor to higher-dimensional conformally symplectic dynamics.
L101: In the present paper, we study the competition between size of the perturbation and strength of attraction, focusing on the study of the regime in which an invariant graph persists, the geometric structure it retains, and the assumptions needed for its regularity.
L102: ### 1.1. Persistence and the Herman–Mather formula
L103: 
L104: When $\phi_{1}=\phi_{2}=0$, the integrable map is
L105: 
L106: (4)  |  | $$F_{\Lambda,\alpha}(x,y)=\bigl(x+\alpha_{1}+\Lambda_{1}y,\,\alpha_{2}+\Lambda_{2}y\bigr).$$  |
L107: 
L108: The contraction assumption implies that $I_{d}-\Lambda_{2}$ is invertible. The unique continuous periodic invariant graph is
L109: 
L110:  | $$\Gamma_{0}:=\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\bigl\{(I_{d}-\Lambda_{2})^{-1}\alpha_{2}\bigr\},$$  |
L111: and its projection on the cylinder attracts every orbit. The induced base map is the rigid translation by
L112: 
L113:  | $$\omega_{0}:=\alpha_{1}+\Lambda_{1}(I_{d}-\Lambda_{2})^{-1}\alpha_{2}.$$  |
L114: On the one hand, the normally hyperbolic invariant manifold theorem [【38†HPS77】] ensures the persistence under sufficiently small perturbations, on the other one, our purpose here is to give explicit bounds that relate the perturbation size to the contraction and the desired regularity of the graph.
L115: We stress the fact that we are not concerned with the control on the tangential dynamics of invariant manifold for which, in the frame of conformally symplectic systems, a KAM-type approach prove that for certain parameters-dependent families of diffeomorphisms or vector fields, invariant tori with prescribed Diophantine dynamics persist under suitable nondegeneracy conditions on the system and appropriate choice of parameters (see for example [【39†CCD13】, 【40†EFK15】, 【41†Mas19】, 【42†CCD22】].
